Posted May 18, 2001

(MarijuanaNews note: My good friend Arnold Trebach founded the Drug Policy Foundation in the 80s when the anti-prohibitionist movement was at a very low ebb. We all owe him a great debt for stepping forward at a time when almost no one would.

He has since retired from the DPF and the American University faculty, but he has not stopped working to end the Drug War. Once again he is stepping forward with something that desperately needs doing. This time his target is one of the most vicious Drug War rackets, one with ties going to the heart of the Republican Party and the Bush Administration.

As the Drug War has become too expensive, and its inhumanity too overwhelming to ignore incompletely, " treatment " has become the new buzz-word. When Bush appointed hardliner John Walters as Drug Czar, he said that the Federal government was going to increase funding for " treatment. " That was supposed to show that this was a " new and improved " prohibition, Drug War Lite. After all, who could be against treatment? And especially as an alternative to prison…
See
The Narking of America: The Bush Team for Total War, or Just to Keep the Lid On.

However, no one ever questions whether " treatment " can be mass-produced like brick for prisons, or if " treatment " was even something that could be defined in any meaningful way.

In fact, there are much more serious questions that need to be asked that are not of a theoretical nature.

Such as -- How could the operators of a notorious rehab racket, Straight Inc., one that targeted children and held them prisoners in incredibly abusive conditions, become major figures in the Republican Party and play a key role in electing George W. Bush President?

Trebach became aware of Straight, Inc. when he was doing research for a book, The Great Drug War. Through that work he met many of the survivors of Straight, Inc.

Ironically, -- as he relates below – he also met the founders of Straight.

In July, he is hosting a conference in Bethesda, MD, in conjunction with a group whose name says it all, The Survivors of Harmful Treatment Programs. The horror stories related by these real-world " Survivors " are much more compelling than anything on " reality television " and raise both ethical and political questions that desperately need to be answered. And once again, Trebach’s timing seems perfect.)

SAVING OUR CHILDREN FROM DRUG TREATMENT ABUSE
A Conference Presented by the Trebach Institute
In Association with The Survivors of Harmful Treatment Programs
PRELIMINARY PROGRAM
July 21-22, 2001
The Marriott Residence Inn
Bethesda, Maryland

Arnold S. Trebach, J.D., Ph.D,.Professor Emeritus, American University
Conference Chair

Last fall, I published an article on my web page titled MORAL INTEGRITY AND PRESIDENTIAL APPOINTEES: The Straight Skinny in which I mention a chance encounter I had years ago in Australia with our then Ambassador to Australia, Melvin Sembler, and his wife, Betty. This occurred at a major international drug conference, attended by leading experts from around the world. Ambassador Sembler was the key speaker at a huge banquet. During the course of his talk, he modestly mentioned that he had a little knowledge about the drug field, having founded a novel juvenile drug rehabilitation in America called Straight, Inc.

Actually I was quite familiar with Straight having investigated it extensively and having devoted an entire chapter of one of my books to the abuses of Straight. In my view -- and that of many other experts -- Straight was a symbol of the destructive ignorance that lay at the heart of our entire approach to drug treatment and control. My wife, Marj, and I were stunned, shocked beyond belief to hear our esteemed ambassador mislead the international audience into believing that one of the horrors of the American drug war was a humane model for the world. We whispered to each other in disbelieving tones which drew puzzled, quiet questions from our distinguished table mates -- what are you so upset about, etc?

We quietly responded and then the Dutch drug czar whispered that, oh yes, he knew about it -- " Hitler jugend! "

Yes, shades of Hitler Youth as the model for the treatment of America's children. Over the intervening years, I did my best to help stop the abuses of Straight and its descendants and relatives. My assumption was that it was pretty much moribund. I have been stunned and shocked again to learn that it and its descendants are still very much alive. My brief Internet article was read by members of an Internet self-help group known loosely as Straight Survivors who contacted me.

After all those years I was saddened to learn that although the original Straight, Inc. may have closed in 1993, there are a number of programs still in existence today which continue to use the Straight methodology. Wes Fager, the father of one of those survivors, has written an on-line book on the Straights called A Clockwork Straight.

From this group I was further dismayed to learn that many other programs in recent years have been accused of child abuse while claiming to treat kids for alcohol and drug abuse, eating problems, sex addiction, and a myriad of other alleged disorders. As a consequence to my corresponding with these Straight survivors and their families on the Internet, I have met with some of them and have joined with them in an effort to expose juvenile and youth treatment programs of all sorts which use destructive or at least questionable treatment tactics.

As a means of beginning to organize our efforts, we are having a conference in July in the greater Washington, DC area to discuss outstanding issues involving these programs to decide what positive actions may be taken to deal with their abuses, including the collection of sworn affidavits from victims and their families. These affidavits may well be delivered to lawyers for consideration of a variety of law suits in those cases where the evidence clearly warrants such action.
